Brush with egg wash and score the top.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) until the pastry is golden and the beef reaches desired doneness, about 25-35 minutes.

dishes.name: Fish and Chips
dishes.description: Battered fried fish with chunky fried potatoes.
steps: Cut potatoes into thick chips, about half an inch wide — thinner cuts will burn before the inside cooks through.

This dish uses a double-fry method for the chips: the first fry cooks the inside through at a lower temperature, and the second fry at a higher temperature crisps the outside. Heat oil to 325°F (160°C) and fry the chips for about 5-6 minutes until soft but pale — not browned yet. Remove and drain.

While the chips rest, make the beer batter: whisk flour with a pinch of baking powder and salt, then whisk in cold beer gradually until you have a smooth batter about the thickness of heavy cream. Cold beer and not overmixing both help keep the batter light and crisp rather than dense.
Increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C) for frying the fish.
Pat the fish fillets completely dry with paper towels — wet fish will make the batter slide off instead of sticking.
Dip each fillet into the batter, letting excess drip off, then carefully lower it into the hot oil away from you to avoid splashing.

Fry the fish for 5-7 minutes, turning once, until the batter is deep golden-brown and crisp, and the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork. Drain on a wire rack, not paper towels, which trap steam and make the bottom soggy.
Increase the oil back to 375°F (190°C) if it dropped, and fry the parboiled chips a second time for 2-3 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Season the chips with salt immediately after removing them from the oil, while they're still hot enough for the salt to stick.
Serve the fish and chips together right away with malt vinegar and tartar sauce — this is a dish that doesn't wait well, since the crispness fades as it cools.

dishes.name: Jerk Chicken
dishes.description: Spicy marinated, smoke-grilled chicken.
steps: Blend scotch bonnet pepper (start with one, or half if you're sensitive to heat), allspice berries, thyme, garlic, ginger, and scallion into a thick, wet marinade paste.
Make several deep cuts into the chicken pieces — this helps the intensely flavored marinade actually penetrate the meat.
Rub the marinade generously all over, working it into the cuts and under the skin. Wear gloves if you can, and avoid touching your face afterward.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Set up your grill for indirect heat — coals or burners on one side only, chicken on the cooler side.
Grill over indirect heat, turning occasionally, for about 35-45 minutes.
In the last 5-10 minutes, move the chicken briefly over direct heat to char the skin, watching closely.
Baste with extra marinade partway through for extra flavor.
Check doneness with a thermometer — chicken should reach 165°F (74°C).
Let rest 5-10 minutes before serving.

dishes.name: Gumbo
dishes.description: Louisiana Creole stew with a deep roux base.
steps: The roux is the foundation and takes patience: heat equal parts oil and flour in a heavy pot over medium-low heat, whisking constantly for 30-45 minutes. You cannot walk away — a roux can burn in under a minute if unattended.
Whisk continuously as the roux moves from pale blonde to peanut-butter brown, to deep chocolate-brown. The darker it gets, the more toasted it tastes and the thinner its thickening power becomes.
Once the roux reaches your desired color, immediately add the diced trinity (onion, celery, bell pepper) — the cold vegetables stop the roux from continuing to darken and burning.
Cook the vegetables in the roux 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add sliced andouille sausage and cook a few more minutes.
Gradually add stock, a ladle at a time, whisking to fully incorporate before adding more.
Add okra and bring to a gentle simmer.
Let it simmer, partially covered, 45 minutes to an hour, stirring occasionally.
In the last 10-15 minutes, add shrimp or chicken, cooking just until done.
Taste and season — often needs a fair amount of salt and a dash of hot sauce.
Serve over steamed rice.

dishes.name: Poutine
dishes.description: Fries topped with cheese curds and hot gravy, a Quebec classic.
steps: Fry potatoes twice — once at a lower temperature to cook through, then again hotter for crispness.
Warm the gravy until simmering.
Pile the hot fries onto a plate or tray.
Scatter cheese curds generously over the fries while they're still hot.
Pour hot gravy over the top so the curds begin to soften, and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Butter Naan
dishes.description: Soft leavened flatbread cooked in a tandoor.
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm milk with a pinch of sugar and let it sit 5-10 minutes until foamy — if it doesn't foam, the yeast may be old, and it's worth starting over.
Mix the yeast mixture with flour, yogurt, and a little oil into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic — this takes longer than it feels like it should, but proper kneading gives naan its chewy texture.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for about an hour, until roughly doubled.
Divide into balls and roll each into an oval, about a quarter-inch thick.
Heat a heavy skillet until very hot.
Place a rolled naan onto the dry, hot skillet — bubbles will form on the surface within a minute or so, your cue it's cooking properly.
Once the bottom browns in spots, flip and cook the other side the same way, until both sides have char spots and the naan is puffed.
Brush the hot naan generously with melted butter as soon as it comes off the pan.
Serve immediately while warm — naan firms up as it cools.

dishes.name: Nihari
dishes.description: Slow-cooked, richly spiced meat stew, often a breakfast dish.
steps: Brown beef shank pieces in ghee with ginger-garlic paste.
Add nihari masala and enough water to cover, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer very slowly for 4-6 hours until the meat is falling-apart tender.
Whisk flour with a little water into a slurry and stir in to thicken the broth.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh ginger, cilantro, and a squeeze of lemon.

dishes.name: Doro Tibs
steps: Sear chicken in hot niter kibbeh until browned.
Add onion and rosemary, cook until softened.
Add jalapeño and berbere if using, cook 5 more minutes.
Serve hot with injera or bread.

dishes.name: Yebeg Tibs (Lamb Tibs)
steps: Sear lamb cubes in hot niter kibbeh until browned.
Add onion and rosemary, cook until softened.
Add jalapeño, cook 5 more minutes until lamb is tender but not overcooked.
Serve sizzling with injera.

dishes.name: Kitcha Fitfit
steps: Cook a thick unleavened flatbread on a dry griddle, then tear into small pieces.
Melt niter kibbeh with berbere.
Toss torn bread in the spiced butter until coated.
Serve warm, often with a side of yogurt.

dishes.name: Kikil
steps: Simmer beef shank in water with onion, garlic, and ginger until very tender, about 1.5 hours.
Stir in turmeric during the last 20 minutes.
Serve in its light broth with injera, often with a squeeze of lemon and awaze on the side.

dishes.name: Kwalima (Eritrean Spiced Sausage)
steps: Mix ground beef thoroughly with berbere and garlic.
Stuff into casings if using, or shape into patties.
Air-dry briefly, then pan-fry or grill until cooked through.
Slice and serve as part of a mixed platter.

dishes.name: Enkulal Firfir (Spiced Scrambled Eggs)
steps: Sauté onion and tomato in niter kibbeh until soft.
Stir in berbere, cook until fragrant.
Add beaten eggs, scramble gently until just set.
Serve warm with bread or injera.

dishes.name: Buticha
steps: Blend cooked chickpeas (or reconstituted chickpea flour) into a smooth paste with a little water.
Mix in lemon juice, minced jalapeño, onion, and olive oil.
Season with salt, serve cold or at room temperature as a dip with injera or bread.

dishes.name: Dinich Wat (Spicy Potato Stew)
steps: Sauté onion in oil until soft.
Add berbere and garlic, cook until fragrant.
Add potatoes and a splash of water, cover and cook 20 min until tender.
Serve with injera.

dishes.name: Awaze Tibs
steps: Sear beef in hot niter kibbeh until browned.
Add onion and rosemary, cook until softened.
Stir in awaze sauce, cook 3-4 more minutes.
Serve hot with injera.

dishes.name: Lasagna
dishes.description: Layered baked pasta dish with meat sauce, cheese, and bechamel.
steps: Brown ground beef and simmer with tomato sauce for 20-30 minutes.
Cook lasagna noodles until just al dente.
Layer noodles, meat sauce, ricotta, and mozzarella in a baking dish, repeating to fill it.
Top the final layer with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) covered for 25 minutes, then uncovered for 15 more until bubbling and golden.

dishes.name: Tiramisu
dishes.description: Coffee-soaked layered dessert with mascarpone cream.
steps: Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale, then fold in mascarpone until smooth.
Whip egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold into the mascarpone mixture.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger in cooled espresso and layer in a dish.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers, then repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and remaining mascarpone.
Dust generously with cocoa powder and chill at least 4 hours before serving.

dishes.name: Enchiladas
dishes.description: Rolled tortillas filled with meat and covered in chili sauce.
steps: Cook chicken until fully cooked, then shred it into bite-sized pieces using two forks.
Toss the shredded chicken with a small amount of enchilada sauce — just enough to lightly coat it, flavoring the filling itself.
Warm the corn tortillas briefly, either in a dry skillet for a few seconds per side or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave for 30 seconds — cold, stiff tortillas will crack when rolled.
Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce across the bottom of a baking dish.
Working with one warm tortilla at a time, place a portion of chicken filling in a line down the center.
Roll the tortilla snugly and place it seam-side down in the dish — this helps it stay closed as it bakes.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas, arranging them snugly next to each other.
Pour the remaining sauce evenly over the top, covering every tortilla completely.
Sprinkle a generous layer of shredded cheese over the top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for about 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and sauce is bubbling.
Let the dish rest 5 minutes before serving.

dishes.name: Guacamole
dishes.description: Mashed avocado dip, a Mexican staple.
steps: Cut 4 ripe avocados in half lengthwise, working around the pit. Twist the two halves apart. To remove the pit safely, either scoop it out with a spoon, or carefully tap a knife blade into it and twist to lift it out — avoid cutting toward your hand.
Scoop the avocado flesh into a bowl using a spoon.

Using a fork (not a blender or food processor — you want texture, not a puree), mash the avocado to your preferred consistency. Some like it smooth, others chunky; there's no wrong answer, just don't overwork it into a paste.
Add 2 tablespoons of fresh lime juice right away and fold it in — this isn't just for flavor, it also slows down browning.
Finely dice a quarter cup of onion, half a cup of tomato, and a small amount of jalapeño (remove the seeds first for less heat). Fold these into the mashed avocado.
Add a small handful of chopped cilantro and a pinch of salt.
Taste and adjust — this is the moment to add more lime for brightness, more salt if it tastes flat, or more jalapeño for more heat.
If not serving immediately, press plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the guacamole (not just over the bowl) to limit air contact, which is what causes browning.
Serve fresh with tortilla chips — guacamole is really best eaten the same day it's made.

dishes.name: Samosa
dishes.description: Fried pastry filled with spiced potatoes and peas.
steps: Make the dough first: mix 2 cups of flour with a pinch of salt and 3 tablespoons of oil, rubbing the oil into the flour until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Gradually add cold water, kneading until firm and smooth — firmer than bread dough, since soft dough makes greasy samosas. Cover and rest 20-30 minutes.
Boil diced potato until just tender, not mushy — you still want some texture. Drain well.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds, let sizzle a few seconds until fragrant. Add peas and boiled potato with garam masala and salt.

Cook the filling a few minutes, mashing some potato with the back of your spoon while leaving other pieces chunky. Let the filling cool completely before assembling — hot filling makes the dough soggy.
Divide the dough into balls, roll each into a thin oval, then cut in half to make two semicircles.
Moisten the straight edge of a semicircle with water. Fold into a cone, overlapping the edges and pressing firmly to seal.
Hold the cone open and spoon in the cooled filling, filling about three-quarters full — leave room to seal the top.
Moisten the remaining open edge and pinch closed, pressing along the seam for no gaps.

Heat oil to medium-low (lower than most frying — samosas need slower cooking so the inside cooks through without the outside burning). Fry a few at a time for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and let cool slightly before eating. Serve with tamarind or mint chutney.

dishes.name: Palak Paneer
dishes.description: Creamy spinach curry with cubes of fresh cheese.
steps: Blanch the spinach: drop it into boiling water for 1-2 minutes until wilted and bright green, then immediately transfer to ice water — this stops the cooking and keeps the vibrant color.
Drain the blanched spinach well and blend it into a smooth puree, adding a splash of water if needed.
Heat oil or ghee and sauté finely diced onion until soft and translucent.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking another minute until fragrant.
Add ground cumin and coriander, stirring 30 seconds to toast the spices.
Pour in the spinach puree and stir to combine.
Simmer about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cut paneer into small cubes. If you have time, lightly pan-fry the cubes until golden on a couple sides for texture contrast.
Gently fold the paneer into the spinach sauce, being careful not to break it up.
Stir in a splash of cream at the end, off the heat.
Serve hot with rice or naan.

dishes.name: Tandoori Chicken
dishes.description: Yogurt-marinated chicken roasted at high heat, traditionally in a tandoor.
steps: Make a few shallow cuts into each piece of chicken — this helps the marinade penetrate deeper, not just sit on the surface.
Whisk together yogurt, tandoori masala, lemon juice, minced garlic, and ginger into a thick, smooth marinade.
Add the chicken and use your hands to work the marinade into every cut and crevice, not just coat the outside.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours — overnight is genuinely worth it, since a short marinade only flavors the surface, while a long one tenderizes and flavors the meat throughout.
Remove the chicken from the fridge about 20 minutes before cooking so it's not ice-cold going into a hot oven or grill.

If using an oven, preheat as hot as it will comfortably go (around 475°F/245°C), and place the chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet so air circulates underneath — this helps it char rather than steam.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once halfway, until edges are charred in spots and a thermometer in the thickest piece reads 165°F (74°C).
If grilling, cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until similarly charred and cooked through, about 20-25 minutes.
Baste with a little melted butter in the last few minutes for extra richness.
Let the chicken rest 5 minutes before serving so the juices redistribute.
Serve with lemon wedges, sliced onion, and mint chutney.

dishes.name: Masala Dosa
dishes.description: Crispy fermented rice-lentil crepe filled with spiced potato.
steps: Sauté mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and cook until soft, then stir in mashed potato with turmeric to make the filling.
Spread a ladle of fermented batter thinly on a hot griddle into a large round.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until crisp and golden underneath.
Spoon the potato filling onto the dosa and fold or roll it closed.

dishes.name: Peking Duck
dishes.description: Roasted duck with crisp skin, served wrapped in thin pancakes.
steps: This dish rewards patience with prep: pat the duck completely dry, then leave it uncovered on a rack in the fridge for several hours, ideally overnight. This air-drying is what gives Peking duck its famously crackling skin — skipping it leaves softer, less crisp skin no matter how well you roast it.
Before roasting, bring a pot of water to a boil and carefully pour it slowly over the duck's skin, or briefly submerge sections — this tightens the skin and helps render fat during roasting.
Mix honey with a splash of water and brush this glaze over the entire duck, then return it to the fridge, uncovered, for another few hours to dry further.
When ready to roast, preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place the duck breast-side up on a rack set over a roasting pan, so fat drips away instead of the duck sitting in it.

Roast for about an hour, then increase the temperature to 425°F (220°C) for the final 15-20 minutes to crisp and darken the skin — watch closely, since the honey glaze can go from caramelized to burnt quickly.
The duck is ready when the skin is a deep, glossy mahogany color and sounds crisp when tapped.
Let the duck rest for 10-15 minutes before carving, so the juices settle.
Carve the crispy skin and some meat into thin slices.
Serve wrapped in warm thin pancakes with hoisin sauce and julienned scallion.

dishes.name: Sweet and Sour Pork
dishes.description: Battered fried pork in a tangy sweet-sour sauce.
steps: Cut pork into bite-sized cubes and toss with a little soy sauce and cornstarch — this thin coating creates the crisp exterior once fried.
Heat oil for deep-frying to about 350°F (175°C). Fry the pork in batches for 4-5 minutes until golden and cooked through. Remove and drain.
In a separate pan, quickly stir-fry bell pepper and pineapple chunks for just a minute or two, keeping them bright and slightly crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk together vinegar, ketchup, sugar, and a splash of water to make the sweet and sour sauce.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the peppers and pineapple, bringing it to a simmer until it thickens slightly.
Add the fried pork and toss quickly to coat evenly — do this fast and right before serving, since letting fried pork sit in sauce softens its crispy coating.
Serve immediately over steamed rice while the pork is still crisp.

dishes.name: Hot and Sour Soup
dishes.description: Tangy, peppery soup balancing heat and sourness.
steps: Bring stock to a simmer with mushrooms and bamboo shoots.
Add tofu and season with soy sauce, vinegar, and white pepper.
Thicken lightly with a cornstarch slurry.
Drizzle in beaten egg slowly while stirring to create thin ribbons.
Taste and adjust the sour-hot balance before serving.

dishes.name: Xiaolongbao (Soup Dumplings)
dishes.description: Steamed dumplings that burst with hot broth inside.
steps: Make the aspic first, since it needs time to set: simmer a rich, gelatin-heavy broth until reduced, then chill until firm, like a wobbly jelly. Chop the set aspic into small cubes — this is what gives xiaolongbao their burst of hot broth, since the aspic melts into liquid once steamed.
Mix ground pork with minced ginger, scallion, soy sauce, and the chopped aspic cubes, stirring gently so you don't crush the aspic pieces.
Make or use dumpling wrappers, rolled thinner at the edges and thicker in the center — this helps hold the weight of the filling and broth without tearing.
Place a spoonful of the pork-and-aspic filling in the center of a wrapper.

This takes the most practice: gather the edges of the wrapper up around the filling, making small pleats around the circumference, then twist and pinch the top closed. If your pleats aren't even at first, that's normal — even a rougher seal will hold the broth as long as it's fully closed.
Place the shaped dumplings into a lined steamer basket, leaving space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes — the aspic melts into broth inside as it steams.
Serve immediately, carefully — these are famously hot inside. Lift one gently onto a spoon, take a small bite to release steam first, then sip the broth before eating the rest.

dishes.name: Tempura
dishes.description: Lightly battered and fried seafood or vegetables.
steps: The key to good tempura is a very cold, barely mixed batter: combine flour and cold egg water (ideally with an ice cube still floating in it) with just a few quick strokes — the batter should look lumpy and streaky with some dry flour visible. Overmixing makes the coating tough and bread-like instead of light and crisp.
Heat oil to 340-350°F (170-175°C) — a thermometer helps a lot here.
Pat your shrimp or vegetable pieces completely dry before dipping — surface moisture makes the batter slide off or causes oil splatter.
Dip each piece into the cold batter, letting excess drip off, then lower it gently into the hot oil.
Fry just a few pieces at a time — overcrowding drops the oil temperature and results in greasy, soggy tempura.
Fry for about 1-2 minutes, until the batter is pale golden (not deep brown, which is overcooked) and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain briefly on a wire rack rather than paper towels.
Serve immediately with a light dipping sauce — tempura loses its crispness quickly.

dishes.name: Tonkatsu
dishes.description: Breaded, deep-fried pork cutlet, a Japanese comfort food.
steps: Pound the pork cutlets to an even thickness using a meat mallet — even thickness means even cooking.
Season the cutlets lightly with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station: flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs in separate dishes.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake off excess, dip in egg, then press firmly into panko so it adheres in an even, thick layer.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) — enough to come about halfway up the side of the cutlet for even frying.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden-brown, checking the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C) for pork.
Drain on a wire rack rather than paper towels, so the bottom doesn't turn soggy.
Let it rest a couple minutes, then slice into strips — this makes it easier to eat and cools it slightly.
Serve with shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce.

dishes.name: Miso Soup
dishes.description: Simple fermented soybean paste soup, a daily staple.
steps: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer.
Add cubed tofu and reconstituted wakame seaweed.
Remove from heat and whisk in miso paste (boiling can dull its flavor).
Stir until the miso is fully dissolved.
Garnish with sliced scallion before serving.

dishes.name: Takoyaki
dishes.description: Ball-shaped savory snack filled with diced octopus.
steps: Heat a takoyaki pan and oil the molds well.
Pour batter into each mold, add a piece of octopus and scallion to each.
As the edges set, use a skewer to rotate each ball a quarter turn, letting raw batter flow in to fill.
Continue rotating until each ball is round and evenly golden.
Drizzle with takoyaki sauce and top with bonito flakes.

dishes.name: Japchae
dishes.description: Stir-fried glass noodles with vegetables, sweet and savory.
steps: Soak sweet potato noodles in warm water for about 30 minutes until pliable, then boil briefly, just 5-6 minutes, until tender but still with a slight chew.
Drain and toss with a little sesame oil and soy sauce right away so they don't stick together.

Cook each vegetable separately in a hot pan, one at a time — spinach quickly wilted, carrot briefly stir-fried, mushroom sautéed until tender. Keeping them separate preserves each ingredient's distinct texture.
Season each vegetable lightly with salt and sesame oil as you cook it.
In the same pan, stir-fry thin beef strips until browned and cooked through.
In a large bowl, combine the noodles, all the vegetables, and the beef.
Add soy sauce, sugar, and a generous amount of sesame oil, then toss everything together thoroughly, making sure the seasoning coats evenly.
Taste and adjust — japchae should taste savory-sweet and nutty.
Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with toasted sesame seeds.

dishes.name: Tteokbokki
dishes.description: Chewy rice cakes in a spicy-sweet sauce, popular street food.
steps: If using refrigerated or frozen rice cakes, soak them in warm water for 10-15 minutes first to soften — skipping this makes them tough.
Bring water or anchovy stock to a simmer in a wide pan.
Whisk in gochujang and a little sugar until fully dissolved.
Add the softened rice cakes and sliced fish cake.

Simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 10-15 minutes — the sauce reduces and thickens while the rice cakes absorb flavor and become chewy and glossy. Don't rush by turning the heat too high, which can burn the sauce before the rice cakes cook through.
If the sauce reduces too much before the rice cakes are tender, add a small splash more liquid and keep simmering.
It's ready when the sauce clings thickly to the rice cakes rather than pooling loosely.
Top with sliced scallion and serve hot, ideally straight from the pan while bubbling.

dishes.name: Massaman Curry
dishes.description: Mild, rich curry with Persian and Indian influences.
steps: Skim the thick cream off unshaken coconut milk and heat it in a pot until it sizzles and separates slightly.
Add massaman curry paste and fry it in the cracked cream for a few minutes, stirring constantly, until deeply fragrant.
Add beef chunks and stir to coat them in the paste, browning the outside slightly.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk with potato and peanuts.
Bring to a simmer, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook gently for about an hour — beef needs this time to become tender, not just heat through.
Check occasionally, stirring gently and adding a splash of water if the sauce reduces too much before the beef is tender.
It's ready when the beef is completely tender and the potato is soft but still holding its shape.
Season with tamarind paste and palm sugar to balance sourness, sweetness, and richness.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

dishes.name: Som Tam (Papaya Salad)
dishes.description: Spicy-sour shredded green papaya salad.
steps: Pound garlic and chili in a mortar to release their oils.
Add green beans and tomato, lightly bruising them.
Add shredded green papaya, pounding and tossing to combine.
Season with lime juice, fish sauce, and a little palm sugar.
Top with crushed peanuts before serving.

dishes.name: Bún Chả
dishes.description: Grilled pork served with rice noodles and herbs in dipping broth.
steps: Grill the pork patties until charred and cooked through.
Cook rice vermicelli and drain.
Warm the fish sauce dipping broth with a little sugar, vinegar, and garlic.
Add the grilled pork to the warm broth.
Serve the noodles and herbs alongside the pork and broth for dipping.

dishes.name: Gado-Gado
dishes.description: Indonesian salad with a rich peanut dressing.

ingredients.name: mixed vegetables (cabbage, green beans, bean sprouts)

ingredient_names: mixed vegetables (cabbage, green beans, bean sprouts)
steps: Blanch or steam the mixed vegetables until just tender.
Fry tofu until golden.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu, and sliced boiled egg on a plate.
Make peanut sauce by blending roasted peanuts with garlic, chili, and a little tamarind and sugar.
Pour the peanut sauce generously over the top before serving.

dishes.name: Satay
dishes.description: Grilled skewered meat served with peanut dipping sauce.
steps: Cut chicken or beef into thin strips, roughly the same size, so they cook evenly and quickly on the skewers.
Marinate the meat in turmeric, minced lemongrass, garlic, and a little oil for at least 30 minutes — turmeric gives it its characteristic golden color.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 20-30 minutes first — this prevents them from burning on the grill.
Thread the marinated meat onto the skewers, weaving it slightly rather than piercing straight through, so it stays secure and cooks evenly.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers, turning every couple of minutes, for about 8-10 minutes total, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
While they cook, make or warm the peanut sauce — blend roasted peanuts with garlic, chili, tamarind, and palm sugar, thinning with water to a dippable consistency.
Serve the hot skewers with peanut sauce for dipping, along with sliced cucumber and rice cakes if you like.

dishes.name: Falafel
dishes.description: Fried chickpea patties, a Levantine staple often served in pita.
steps: Start with dried chickpeas, not canned — canned chickpeas have too much moisture and will make your falafel fall apart or turn gummy when fried. Soak 2 cups of dried chickpeas in plenty of water for at least 12 hours or overnight.
Drain the soaked chickpeas well and pat fairly dry.

In a food processor, combine the chickpeas with garlic, chopped parsley and cilantro, cumin, and coriander. Pulse — don't puree — until finely chopped and holding together when pressed, but still with visible texture, like coarse sand. A smooth paste will be too dense and won't fry properly.
Transfer to a bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes — this firms it up and makes shaping much easier.
Just before frying, mix in a small amount of baking soda, which helps the falafel puff up slightly for a lighter texture inside.
Shape the mixture into balls or small patties, about the size of a golf ball.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C) — test by dropping in a small piece; it should sizzle immediately and rise to the surface, not sink.
Fry in small batches (don't crowd the pot) for 3-4 minutes, until deeply golden-brown and crisp outside.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm in pita with tahini sauce, pickles, and fresh vegetables.

dishes.name: Fattoush
dishes.description: Crisp salad topped with toasted or fried pita chips.
steps: Break toasted or fried pita into crouton-sized pieces.
Combine mixed greens, tomato, and cucumber in a large bowl.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, and sumac into a dressing.
Toss the salad with the dressing just before serving.
Scatter the pita pieces on top so they stay crisp.

dishes.name: Mujadara
dishes.description: Simple lentil and rice dish topped with crispy onions.
steps: Cook lentils in water until just tender, about 20 minutes.
Fry sliced onion in oil until deeply caramelized and crispy, then set aside.
Add rice and cumin to the cooked lentils with the right amount of water, and cook until the rice is tender.
Fluff the rice and lentils together.
Top generously with the crispy fried onions before serving.

dishes.name: Menemen
dishes.description: Turkish scrambled eggs cooked with tomato and peppers.
steps: Sauté onion and green pepper until softened.
Add diced tomato and cook until it breaks down into a light sauce.
Crack eggs directly into the pan.
Stir gently, scrambling the eggs into the tomato mixture, until just set.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.

dishes.name: Lahmacun
dishes.description: Thin, crispy flatbread topped with spiced minced meat.
steps: Mix ground lamb with diced tomato, minced onion, parsley, and spices to make a loose, spreadable topping.
Roll dough very thin into rounds.
Spread the meat mixture thinly and evenly over each round, right to the edges.
Bake at very high heat until the crust is crisp and the meat is cooked, about 8-10 minutes.
Squeeze fresh lemon over the top and roll up to eat.

dishes.name: Tahdig
dishes.description: Persian rice with a coveted crispy golden crust.
steps: Parboil rice until just shy of tender, then drain.
Mix a portion of the rice with yogurt and saffron water to make a base layer.
Spread this mixture in a thin layer over the bottom of a well-oiled pot.
Mound the remaining rice on top in a pyramid shape and drizzle with melted butter.
Cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes until a golden crust forms on the bottom, then invert onto a platter.

dishes.name: Kebab Koobideh
dishes.description: Seasoned ground meat kebabs, a Persian grilling classic.
steps: Mix ground meat with grated onion (squeezed of excess liquid), salt, and pepper until sticky and well combined.
Mold the mixture tightly around flat skewers into long, thin shapes.
Grill over hot coals, turning occasionally, until charred outside and cooked through.
Brush with saffron butter partway through.
Serve with grilled tomato and rice, dusted with sumac.

dishes.name: Harira
dishes.description: Hearty tomato-based soup, traditionally eaten to break the Ramadan fast.
steps: Brown lamb pieces with onion and warming spices.
Add crushed tomato, lentils, and stock, then simmer 30 minutes.
Add cooked chickpeas and continue simmering until the lentils are tender.
Thicken slightly with a flour-water mixture if desired.
Finish with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lemon.

dishes.name: Pastilla
dishes.description: Sweet-savory pie layering spiced meat and almonds in flaky pastry.

ingredients.name: chicken or pigeon, cooked and shredded

ingredient_names: chicken or pigeon, cooked and shredded
steps: Cook and shred the meat, mixing with warming spices.
Toast almonds and toss with sugar and cinnamon.
Layer sheets of phyllo in a round pan, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread the meat filling and top with the sweet almond mixture, then fold the phyllo over to seal.
Bake until golden, then dust the top with powdered sugar and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Pepper Soup
dishes.description: Light, fiery peppery broth, often used as a warming remedy.
steps: Combine meat, spice blend, scotch bonnet, and onion in a pot with water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the meat is tender, 45 minutes to an hour.
Skim any foam that rises to the top.
Adjust seasoning and heat level to taste.
Serve hot in bowls as a light, warming soup.

dishes.name: Moin Moin
dishes.description: Steamed bean pudding, often wrapped in leaves or foil.
steps: Blend soaked and peeled beans with pepper and onion into a smooth batter.
Whisk in palm oil and season with salt and stock cube.
Pour the batter into small foil or leaf-lined molds, adding a slice of egg to each.
Steam the molds for about an hour until firm and set.
Unmold and serve warm.

dishes.name: Banku
dishes.description: Fermented, cooked dough staple, eaten with soup or stew.
steps: Mix the fermented dough with water in a pot.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden paddle.
Continue cooking and stirring until the mixture becomes smooth, thick, and stretchy, 15-20 minutes.
Wet your hands and shape into smooth balls.
Serve with soup or stew and a side of pepper sauce.

dishes.name: Kelewele
dishes.description: Spiced, fried plantain cubes, a popular Ghanaian street snack.
steps: Toss cubed plantain with grated ginger, cayenne, ground cloves, and a little salt.
Let it marinate for about 10 minutes.
Heat oil until hot.
Fry the seasoned plantain in batches until deeply golden and caramelized at the edges.
Drain and serve hot as a snack.

dishes.name: Sukuma Wiki
dishes.description: Simple sautéed greens, a daily staple across East Africa.
steps: Sauté onion in oil until soft.
Add diced tomato and cook briefly.
Add shredded collard greens in batches, letting each wilt before adding more.
Cook until tender but still bright green, about 10 minutes.
Season with salt and serve alongside ugali.

dishes.name: Biltong
dishes.description: Air-dried, cured meat snack, similar to jerky but distinct in seasoning.
steps: Coat beef strips in vinegar, then season generously with crushed coriander and salt.
Let the meat cure in the fridge for a few hours.
Hang the strips in a well-ventilated, cool, dry space (or use a dehydrator).
Air-dry for several days until firm and dark, checking periodically for desired chewiness.
Slice thinly against the grain to serve.

dishes.name: Brigadeiro
dishes.description: Fudgy chocolate truffle, a staple at Brazilian celebrations.
steps: Combine condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the pan, about 10 minutes.
Let the mixture cool completely.
Roll into small balls with buttered hands.
Coat each ball in chocolate sprinkles.

dishes.name: Pão de Queijo
dishes.description: Chewy, cheesy baked bread rolls.
steps: Heat milk and oil together until just simmering.
Pour over tapioca flour and mix until a sticky dough forms.
Let cool slightly, then beat in eggs and grated cheese.
Shape into small balls and place on a baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes until puffed and golden.

dishes.name: Moqueca
dishes.description: Brazilian fish stew simmered in coconut milk and palm oil.
steps: Sauté onion, garlic, and bell pepper until softened.
Add tomato and cook until it breaks down slightly.
Add coconut milk and palm oil, bringing to a gentle simmer.
Add fish pieces and poach gently in the sauce until just cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Finish with fresh cilantro before serving with rice.

dishes.name: Asado
dishes.description: Argentine barbecue tradition centered on slow-grilled meats.

ingredients.name: mixed cuts of beef (short rib, flank)

ingredient_names: mixed cuts of beef (short rib, flank)
steps: Season the meat generously with coarse salt.
Build a wood or charcoal fire and let it burn down to steady coals.
Grill the meat slowly over indirect heat, turning occasionally, until deeply browned and cooked through — this can take 1-2 hours for larger cuts.
Rest the meat briefly before slicing.
Serve with chimichurri on the side.

dishes.name: Lomo Saltado
dishes.description: Peruvian stir-fry blending Chinese and Latin American technique.
steps: Stir-fry beef strips quickly in a very hot pan or wok until browned, then remove.
Stir-fry onion and tomato briefly, keeping some bite.
Return the beef to the pan with soy sauce and a splash of vinegar, tossing to coat.
Fold in freshly fried french fries at the very end so they stay crisp.
Serve immediately over rice.

dishes.name: Tortilla Española
dishes.description: Thick Spanish potato and egg omelette.
steps: Peel 4 medium potatoes and slice them thin (about an eighth of an inch) — a mandoline makes this easier and more even.
Thinly slice 1 onion as well.
Heat a generous amount of olive oil (about a cup) in a wide, non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add the potato and onion.

Cook slowly, stirring gently every few minutes, for 20-25 minutes. You're not frying to crisp — you want them fully soft and tender, almost falling apart, without browning. Lower the heat if they start to color.
Drain the potato and onion in a colander over a bowl, reserving the flavorful oil for later.
Beat 6 eggs well in a large bowl. Add the drained, warm potato and onion, gently folding together, lightly breaking up some slices as you mix.
Let this sit 5-10 minutes; the warm potatoes gently season the eggs and help everything cook more evenly.
Wipe out the pan, add a couple tablespoons of the reserved oil, heat over medium. Pour in the mixture, spread evenly, reduce heat to medium-low.
Cook about 5 minutes until edges are set and the bottom is golden — gently shake the pan to check it moves as one piece.

Place a large plate over the pan and, holding both firmly together, flip so the tortilla lands on the plate. Slide it back into the pan uncooked-side down to finish for another 3-4 minutes. Don't worry if it looks messy the first time — even an uneven flip still tastes great.
Slide onto a serving plate and rest a few minutes before slicing. Traditionally served warm or at room temperature.

dishes.name: Churros
dishes.description: Fried dough pastry, crisp outside and soft inside.
steps: Bring water, butter, and salt to a boil, then stir in flour to form a thick dough.
Beat in eggs one at a time until smooth and glossy.
Pipe strips of dough directly into hot oil.
Fry until deeply golden, turning as needed.
Toss the hot churros in cinnamon sugar before serving.

dishes.name: Spanakopita
dishes.description: Flaky pastry filled with spinach and feta.
steps: Squeeze out as much liquid as possible from cooked spinach using a clean kitchen towel — watery filling will make the phyllo soggy no matter how well you bake it.
Mix the well-drained spinach with crumbled feta, a beaten egg, and fresh dill.
Keep your phyllo sheets covered with a slightly damp towel while you work, since they dry out and crack within minutes.
Brush a baking dish with melted butter, then layer about half your phyllo sheets in, brushing each individual sheet with butter.
Spread the spinach and feta filling evenly over the buttered phyllo base.
Layer the remaining phyllo on top, again brushing each sheet with butter.
Before baking, score the top layers into squares or triangles with a sharp knife — this makes it much easier to cut cleanly once baked.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for about 35-40 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp on top.
Let cool at least 10-15 minutes before cutting along the scored lines, so the filling sets and doesn't run out.

dishes.name: Quiche Lorraine
dishes.description: Savory egg custard tart with bacon and cheese.
steps: If making your own pastry, roll it out and line a tart pan, pressing gently into the corners without stretching. Prick the bottom with a fork and chill for 20-30 minutes.

Blind bake the crust: line it with parchment and fill with pie weights, then bake at 375°F (190°C) for about 15 minutes. Remove the weights and parchment and bake another 5-8 minutes until lightly golden — this keeps the bottom from turning soggy once the wet filling is added.
While the crust bakes, cook diced bacon until crisp, then drain.
Scatter the crisp bacon and a generous amount of grated gruyere evenly over the bottom of the pre-baked crust.
Whisk eggs with cream and a small pinch of nutmeg until well combined.
Pour the egg mixture slowly and evenly over the bacon and cheese, filling nearly to the top.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 30-35 minutes, until the filling is just set — a slight jiggle in the very center is correct, similar to a baked custard.
Let cool for at least 10-15 minutes before slicing so the custard finishes setting.

dishes.name: Croissant
dishes.description: Flaky, buttery layered pastry, a French breakfast staple.
steps: This project takes real time across a couple of days, so plan accordingly. Make a basic yeasted dough, keeping it fairly firm, then wrap and refrigerate for at least an hour.
While the dough chills, pound a block of cold butter between parchment paper into a flat, even rectangle — keep the butter cold throughout, re-refrigerating if it starts softening.
Roll the chilled dough into a rectangle roughly twice the size of your butter block. Place the butter in the center and fold the dough over from both sides, fully encasing it.
Roll this dough-butter package into a long rectangle, then fold it into thirds like a letter — this is a 'turn.' Wrap and chill 30-45 minutes.

Repeat this rolling-and-folding turn two more times, chilling between each — this lamination process is what creates the many thin layers responsible for a croissant's flaky texture. Rushing this or letting the butter get too warm will cause it to break through instead of staying in distinct layers.
After the final turn and chill, roll the dough into a large, thin rectangle and cut it into triangles.
Roll each triangle up from the wide base to the point, curving the ends slightly inward into the classic crescent shape.
Place the shaped croissants on a baking sheet and let them proof in a warm spot for 1.5-2 hours, until visibly puffy and jiggly when the pan is gently shaken.
Brush with egg wash and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 18-20 minutes, until deeply golden and the layers are visibly flaky.

dishes.name: Sauerbraten
dishes.description: Marinated pot roast, Germany's traditional sour braised beef.
steps: Marinate the beef in vinegar, water, onion, and juniper berries in the refrigerator for 2-3 days, turning occasionally.
Remove the beef and pat dry, reserving the marinade.
Sear the beef on all sides in a hot pot.
Add the strained marinade and simmer covered for 2.5-3 hours until tender.
Thicken the sauce with crushed gingersnaps before serving, sliced, with the gravy.

dishes.name: Currywurst
dishes.description: Sliced sausage doused in curry-spiced ketchup, a Berlin street food icon.
steps: Grill or pan-fry the sausages until browned and cooked through.
Simmer ketchup with curry powder and worcestershire sauce for a few minutes to build a sauce.
Slice the cooked sausages into bite-sized pieces.
Pour the curry sauce over the sliced sausage.
Dust with extra curry powder and serve with fries.

dishes.name: Pelmeni
dishes.description: Small boiled dumplings filled with seasoned meat.
steps: Make a simple dough from flour, egg, and water, then rest it.
Mix ground meat with minced onion, salt, and pepper.
Roll dough thin and cut into small rounds.
Place a small amount of filling in each round and fold into a dumpling, pinching the corners together.
Boil in salted water until they float, about 5-7 minutes, and serve with sour cream.

dishes.name: Beef Stroganoff
dishes.description: Sautéed beef in a creamy mushroom sauce, served over noodles or rice.
steps: Sear beef strips quickly in a hot pan, then set aside.
Sauté onion and mushrooms in the same pan until browned.
Add broth and simmer briefly, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in sour cream off the heat and return the beef to warm through.
Serve over cooked egg noodles.

dishes.name: Shepherd's Pie
dishes.description: Baked minced meat topped with mashed potato.
steps: Peel and quarter potatoes, then boil in salted water until completely tender when pierced with a fork, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
While the potatoes cook, brown ground lamb in a large pan with diced onion and carrot, breaking the meat up as it cooks.
Once browned, sprinkle a couple tablespoons of flour over the meat and stir it in — this thin coating is what thickens the gravy once liquid is added, so don't skip it.
Pour in beef stock gradually, stirring as you go to avoid lumps, then add peas.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until the mixture thickens into a rich, saucy filling — not soupy, and not dry. It should hold its shape on a spoon but still look moist.
Mash the drained potatoes with butter and warm milk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the meat filling evenly into a baking dish.
Spoon the mashed potato over the top, spreading it to cover the filling completely and sealing the edges — any gaps will let the filling bubble up and burn during baking.
For a nicer finish, drag a fork across the surface of the potato to create ridges — the ridges crisp up beautifully in the oven.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden-brown in spots and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
Let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving so the filling sets slightly and doesn't run everywhere when you scoop it.

dishes.name: Mac and Cheese
dishes.description: Creamy baked or stovetop pasta and cheese classic.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the macaroni until just al dente, following the package timing — it will cook a little more in the oven if baking, so don't overdo it here. Drain and set aside.
In a separate saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat.

Once melted, whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly — this cooks out the raw flour taste and forms the base (a roux) for your sauce. It should look like a thick paste and smell lightly toasted, not raw.
Gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time at first, whisking continuously to prevent lumps. Once about half the milk is in and the mixture is smooth, you can add the rest more quickly.
Keep whisking over medium heat until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 5-6 minutes. It should be noticeably thicker than milk but still pourable.
Remove from heat and stir in the shredded cheddar a handful at a time, letting each addition melt fully before adding more — this keeps the sauce smooth instead of grainy.
Season with a pinch of salt, black pepper, and if you like, a small pinch of mustard powder or cayenne for depth (optional but recommended).
Add the drained macaroni to the cheese sauce and stir until every piece is coated.

If baking: transfer to a greased baking dish, top with breadcrumbs, and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. If serving straight from the stovetop, it's ready to eat right away.
Let it sit for a couple of minutes before serving — the sauce continues to thicken slightly as it cools.

dishes.name: Buffalo Wings
dishes.description: Fried chicken wings tossed in spicy butter sauce.
steps: Pat the chicken wings completely dry with paper towels — this is the single most important step for crispy wings, whether frying or baking. Any surface moisture will steam instead of crisp.
If you have time, leave the wings uncovered on a rack in the fridge for an hour or more before cooking — this air-dries the skin further for extra crispness.

To fry: heat oil to 375°F (190°C). Fry the wings in batches (don't crowd the pot, which drops the oil temperature) for 8-10 minutes, until deeply golden and cooked through, with an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C).
To bake instead: place wings on a wire rack set over a baking sheet (the rack lets air circulate underneath) and bake at 425°F (220°C) for 40-45 minutes, flipping halfway through.
While the wings cook, make the sauce: melt butter in a small saucepan and whisk in hot sauce until fully combined and glossy.
As soon as the wings come out of the fryer or oven, transfer them immediately to a large bowl while they're still hot — hot wings absorb the sauce better than cooled ones.
Pour the sauce over the wings and toss thoroughly, either with tongs or by covering the bowl and shaking, until every wing is evenly coated.
Serve immediately with blue cheese or ranch dip and celery sticks — buffalo wings are best eaten right away while the coating is still glossy and hot.

dishes.name: Chicken Adobo
dishes.description: Braised chicken in soy sauce and vinegar, the Philippines' de facto national dish.
steps: Combine chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Uncover and continue simmering until the sauce reduces and thickens, about 15 more minutes.
Optionally, pan-sear the chicken pieces separately for extra color, then return to the sauce.
Serve with steamed rice.

dishes.name: Laksa
dishes.description: Spicy coconut curry noodle soup blending Chinese and Malay flavors.
steps: Fry the laksa curry paste in a little oil over medium heat for a few minutes until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and enough stock or water to reach a soup-like consistency, then bring to a simmer.
Add shrimp or chicken and tofu puffs, simmering until the protein is fully cooked, about 8-10 minutes.
While the broth simmers, cook rice noodles separately, then drain.
Divide the cooked noodles among serving bowls.
Ladle the hot broth generously over the noodles, making sure everyone gets a good mix of shrimp, tofu puffs, and broth.
Top with fresh bean sprouts and a few sprigs of laksa leaf or cilantro if you have it.
Serve immediately while the broth is hot, since noodles keep absorbing liquid the longer they sit.

dishes.name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
dishes.description: Poached chicken served with rice cooked in chicken fat and broth.
steps: Poach the whole chicken gently in water with ginger and scallion until just cooked through, then rest in ice water to firm the skin.
Reserve the poaching liquid as stock.
Sauté garlic and a little ginger, then toast the rice briefly before cooking it in the reserved chicken stock.
Chop the chicken into pieces.
Serve the rice and chicken together with chili sauce and ginger-scallion sauce on the side.

dishes.name: Arancini
dishes.description: Fried, breaded risotto balls, a Sicilian street food staple.
steps: Take a handful of chilled risotto and flatten it in your palm.
Place a cube of mozzarella in the center and mold the rice around it into a ball.
Dredge each ball in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Deep fry until golden and crisp all over.
Drain and serve warm.

dishes.name: Focaccia
dishes.description: Flat oven-baked Italian bread, dimpled and drizzled with olive oil.
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water and let it foam.
Mix with flour and a portion of the olive oil into a soft, sticky dough.
Let rise for about an hour until doubled.
Press the dough into an oiled pan, dimpling it all over with your fingers.
Drizzle with more olive oil, scatter rosemary and salt, then bake at 425°F (220°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden.

dishes.name: Panzanella
dishes.description: Tuscan bread and tomato salad, a way to use up day-old bread.
steps: Toast or lightly char the stale bread cubes if not already very dry.
Combine bread with chopped tomato, cucumber, and red onion.
Whisk olive oil and vinegar together.
Toss the salad with the dressing.
Let it sit 15-20 minutes before serving so the bread absorbs the juices.

dishes.name: Caprese Salad
dishes.description: Simple sliced tomato and mozzarella salad in the colors of the Italian flag.
steps: Slice tomato and mozzarella into even rounds.
Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a plate.
Tuck fresh basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Season with salt and black pepper before serving.

dishes.name: Pesto alla Genovese
dishes.description: Bright, herby sauce from Liguria, traditionally pounded in a mortar.
steps: Toast pine nuts lightly in a dry pan.
Blend or pound basil, pine nuts, and garlic together.
Gradually work in the olive oil until a thick paste forms.
Stir in grated parmesan by hand.
Toss with hot pasta, thinning with a little pasta water if needed.

dishes.name: Cassoulet
dishes.description: Slow-cooked white bean casserole from southwestern France.
steps: Simmer soaked beans with onion and aromatics until nearly tender.
Brown the pork shoulder and sausage separately.
Layer beans, pork, sausage, and duck confit in a large casserole.
Add enough bean cooking liquid to just cover.
Bake uncovered at 300°F (150°C) for 2-3 hours, breaking and pressing the crust that forms back in occasionally.

dishes.name: Bouillabaisse
dishes.description: Provençal fish stew from the port city of Marseille.
steps: Sauté fennel and onion in olive oil until softened.
Add crushed tomato, saffron, and fish stock, then bring to a simmer.
Add firmer fish first, simmering a few minutes, then add delicate fish and shellfish last.
Simmer gently just until everything is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Serve with toasted bread and rouille sauce.

dishes.name: Croque Monsieur
dishes.description: Grilled ham and cheese sandwich topped with bechamel sauce.
steps: Spread a thin layer of bechamel on each slice of bread.
Layer ham and grated gruyere between two slices to make a sandwich.
Top the outside with more bechamel and a layer of cheese.
Grill or bake until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the bread is golden.
Slice and serve hot.

dishes.name: Salade Niçoise
dishes.description: Composed salad from Nice with tuna, olives, and hard-boiled egg.
steps: Arrange lettuce on a large platter as a base.
Group tuna, green beans, sliced egg, olives, tomato, and potato in separate sections over the lettuce.
Drizzle with a simple vinaigrette of olive oil, lemon, and dijon mustard.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve at room temperature, tossing gently at the table if desired.

dishes.name: French Onion Soup
dishes.description: Rich onion soup topped with melted cheese over toasted bread.
steps: Cook sliced onions slowly in butter over low heat until deeply caramelized, 30-40 minutes.
Add beef broth and simmer 20 minutes.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls.
Top each with a slice of toasted baguette and a generous layer of grated gruyere.
Broil until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

dishes.name: Duck Confit
dishes.description: Duck slow-cooked and preserved in its own fat until tender.
steps: Rub duck legs generously with coarse salt, garlic, and thyme, then cure in the fridge for at least 12 hours.
Rinse and pat the duck legs dry.
Submerge the legs completely in melted duck fat in a baking dish.
Cook low and slow at 225°F (110°C) for about 2.5-3 hours until very tender.
Crisp the skin in a hot pan just before serving.

dishes.name: Patatas Bravas
dishes.description: Fried potato cubes served with a spicy sauce, a classic Spanish tapa.
steps: Fry or roast cubed potatoes until crisp and golden outside, tender within.
Make the bravas sauce by simmering tomato sauce with smoked paprika and cayenne.
Pile the hot potatoes on a plate.
Spoon the spicy tomato sauce over the top.
Finish with a drizzle of aioli.

dishes.name: Pisto
dishes.description: Spanish vegetable medley similar to ratatouille, often topped with a fried egg.
steps: Sauté onion and bell pepper in olive oil until softened.
Add zucchini and cook until tender.
Add diced tomato and simmer until everything melds into a thick, stewed mixture, about 20 minutes.
Season with salt.
Serve warm, often topped with a fried egg.

dishes.name: Fabada Asturiana
dishes.description: Hearty bean stew from Asturias with cured meats.
steps: Simmer soaked beans with pork shoulder in plenty of water until beans begin to soften, about an hour.
Add chorizo, morcilla, and saffron.
Continue simmering gently until the beans and meats are fully tender, another hour, adding water as needed.
Avoid vigorous stirring, which can break the beans; shake the pot instead.
Serve hot in deep bowls.

dishes.name: Bacalhau à Brás
dishes.description: Shredded salt cod scrambled with potato straws and egg.
steps: Soak salt cod for 24 hours, changing the water several times, then shred it.
Fry matchstick potatoes until golden and crisp.
Sauté onion until soft, then add shredded cod and cook briefly.
Add the fried potatoes and beaten eggs, stirring gently until the eggs are just set but still creamy.
Garnish with olives and parsley before serving.

dishes.name: Caldo Verde
dishes.description: Portuguese green soup with shredded kale and sliced sausage.
steps: Simmer potato and onion in water or stock until very soft.
Blend or mash until smooth to form the soup base.
Return to the pot and bring back to a simmer.
Add thinly shredded kale and sliced chorizo, cooking just a few minutes until the kale is tender.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil before serving.

dishes.name: Pastel de Nata
dishes.description: Portuguese custard tart with a flaky, caramelized top.
steps: Line muffin tins with rounds of puff pastry, pressing up the sides.
Warm milk with a cinnamon stick, then whisk in sugar and egg yolks.
Strain the custard and pour into the pastry shells.
Bake at a very high temperature (500°F/260°C) until the custard is set with dark caramelized spots on top, about 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly before serving, dusted with cinnamon.

dishes.name: Francesinha
dishes.description: Porto's indulgent layered sandwich smothered in a spicy tomato-beer sauce.
steps: Layer bread with a mix of ham, sausage, and steak.
Cover completely with sliced cheese.
Bake or broil until the cheese melts and blankets the sandwich.
Simmer a sauce of beer, tomato, and a little piri-piri until rich and slightly thickened, then pour over the sandwich.
Top with a fried egg and serve with fries.

dishes.name: Bratwurst
dishes.description: Grilled German sausage, often served with mustard and a roll.
steps: Simmer bratwurst gently in beer with onions for about 10 minutes (optional but classic).
Finish the sausages on a hot grill until browned and crisp outside.
Toast a bread roll.
Serve the sausage in the roll with mustard and the cooked onions.

dishes.name: Pretzel
dishes.description: Chewy, knot-shaped German bread with a distinctive dark crust.
steps: Make a yeasted dough with flour and warm water, then let it rise about an hour.
Divide and roll into long ropes, then shape into the classic pretzel knot.
Briefly boil each pretzel in water with baking soda dissolved in it — this gives the dark, chewy crust.
Place on a baking sheet and sprinkle with coarse salt.
Bake at 450°F (230°C) until deep golden brown, about 12-15 minutes.

dishes.name: Kartoffelsalat
dishes.description: German potato salad, served warm with a tangy vinegar dressing.
steps: Boil potatoes until just tender, then slice while still warm.
Whisk vinegar, warm broth, and mustard together for the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the warm potato slices so they absorb it.
Add diced onion and toss gently.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

dishes.name: Black Forest Cake
dishes.description: Layered chocolate cake with cherries and cream, named after the Black Forest region.
steps: Bake chocolate sponge cake layers and let them cool.
Soak the layers lightly with kirsch (cherry brandy).
Whip cream and spread between the layers along with cherries.
Stack the layers, frosting the outside with more whipped cream.
Decorate with chocolate shavings and whole cherries.

dishes.name: Irish Stew
dishes.description: Simple, hearty lamb and root vegetable stew.
steps: Brown lamb pieces in a large pot.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Add stock, carrot, and potato.
Cover and simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours until the meat is tender and the potatoes have thickened the broth.
Season and serve hot with crusty bread.

dishes.name: Haggis
dishes.description: Scotland's savory pudding of seasoned offal and oats, traditionally served with neeps and tatties.
steps: Simmer the offal in water until cooked through, then mince finely.
Toast the oats lightly in a dry pan.
Combine minced offal, toasted oats, minced onion, and suet with enough stock to bind.
Season generously with black pepper and traditional spices.
Pack tightly into a casing (or baking dish) and steam for 2-3 hours until firm.

dishes.name: Bangers and Mash
dishes.description: British comfort food pairing sausages with mashed potato and gravy.
steps: Boil potatoes until very tender, then drain.
Mash the potatoes with butter and warm milk until smooth.
Grill or pan-fry the sausages until browned and cooked through.
Warm the onion gravy.
Serve the sausages over mashed potato, topped generously with gravy.

dishes.name: Stroopwafel
dishes.description: Thin waffle cookies sandwiched with a caramel filling.
steps: Make a rich, slightly sweet yeasted dough and let it rest.
Divide into small balls and press each in a hot waffle iron until thin and golden.
While still warm, slice each waffle in half horizontally.
Spread caramel syrup filling on the cut side of one half.
Sandwich with the other half, pressing gently to seal.

dishes.name: Moules Frites
dishes.description: Steamed mussels served with a side of crispy fries, Belgium's signature dish.
steps: Sauté shallot in butter until soft.
Add white wine and bring to a simmer.
Add cleaned mussels, cover, and steam until they open, about 5-7 minutes, discarding any that stay closed.
Fry potatoes until golden and crisp.
Serve the mussels in their broth alongside a big portion of fries.

dishes.name: Bitterballen
dishes.description: Deep-fried Dutch meat croquettes, a popular bar snack.
steps: Make a very thick, well-seasoned beef ragout, then chill it until firm.
Shape the cold ragout into small balls.
Dredge each ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Deep fry until deeply golden and crisp.
Serve hot with mustard for dipping.

dishes.name: Cheese Fondue
dishes.description: Melted cheese shared communally, eaten by dipping bread on long forks.
steps: Rub the inside of a fondue pot with a cut garlic clove.
Heat white wine gently, then gradually melt in grated gruyere and emmental, stirring constantly.
Toss the cheese with a little cornstarch first to help it stay smooth.
Keep the pot warm over a low flame at the table.
Dip cubes of bread on long forks, swirling to keep the cheese moving.

dishes.name: Raclette
dishes.description: Melted cheese scraped over potatoes and accompaniments, both a dish and a social meal.
steps: Boil small potatoes until tender.
Slice raclette cheese and melt it under a broiler or in a raclette grill.
Pour the melted cheese over the warm potatoes.
Serve with cured meats, cornichons, and pickled onions on the side.
Repeat with fresh cheese and potatoes throughout the meal, as raclette is eaten in rounds.

dishes.name: Sachertorte
dishes.description: Dense Viennese chocolate cake with a thin layer of apricot jam.
steps: Bake a dense chocolate sponge cake.
Slice the cake in half and spread a thin layer of apricot jam in the middle.
Reassemble and coat the whole cake with more apricot jam.
Pour a glossy chocolate glaze over the top, letting it drip down the sides.
Let the glaze set before slicing and serving, traditionally with whipped cream.

dishes.name: Gyro
dishes.description: Greek wrapped sandwich of spiced meat, similar in spirit to shawarma and doner.
steps: If making the meat from scratch rather than buying pre-seasoned, marinate thin-sliced lamb or chicken in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and oregano for at least an hour.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over high heat.

Cook the marinated meat in batches, without crowding the pan, until well charred on the edges and cooked through — about 3-4 minutes per side for thin slices, checking that chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) internally.

While the meat cooks, make a quick tzatziki if you don't have store-bought: grate a cucumber and squeeze out as much excess water as possible using a clean towel (this step matters — skip it and your tzatziki will be watery), then mix with yogurt, minced garlic, a little lemon juice, and chopped dill.
Warm the pita bread briefly in a dry pan or over a flame until soft and pliable, not stiff.
Spread a generous layer of tzatziki inside each pita.
Pile in the warm, charred meat.
Top with sliced tomato, thinly sliced onion, and a little more tzatziki if you like.
Wrap the pita around the filling, folding one end up to prevent everything from falling out the bottom, and serve immediately while the meat is still hot.

dishes.name: Greek Salad
dishes.description: Simple salad of tomato, cucumber, olives, and feta, no lettuce involved.
steps: Cut tomato into large wedges and cucumber into thick half-moons — this salad has substantial, chunky pieces, not finely diced vegetables.
Thinly slice red onion.
Combine tomato, cucumber, and onion in a large bowl, along with Kalamata olives.
Rather than crumbling the feta, place a large, thick slab of it directly on top of the salad — this is the traditional presentation.
Drizzle generously with good olive oil, letting it pool slightly at the bottom.
Sprinkle dried oregano over the top, especially over the feta.
Season with a little salt (go easy, since the olives and feta are already salty) and cracked black pepper.
Serve immediately without tossing beforehand — let each person break into the feta and mix the salad at the table.

dishes.name: Ćevapi
dishes.description: Grilled minced meat fingers popular across the former Yugoslavia.
steps: Mix ground meats with garlic, baking soda, and salt, kneading well to develop a springy texture.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for a few hours or overnight.
Shape into small finger-sized sausages.
Grill over high heat, turning often, until charred outside and cooked through.
Serve in warm flatbread with chopped onion.

dishes.name: Burek
dishes.description: Flaky spiral or layered pastry filled with meat, cheese, or spinach.
steps: Cook ground beef with minced onion until browned, then let it cool.
Layer sheets of phyllo, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread a portion of the meat filling and roll into a coil, or layer flat depending on style.
Coil the filled rolls into a spiral in a round pan, or cut into portions.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until deeply golden and crisp, about 35-40 minutes.

dishes.name: Sarmale
dishes.description: Romanian cabbage rolls stuffed with spiced meat and rice.
steps: Mix ground pork with rice, minced onion, and seasoning.
Place a spoonful of filling on each blanched cabbage leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Layer the rolls snugly in a large pot.
Cover with tomato sauce and enough water to just cover.
Simmer gently for 1.5-2 hours until the rice is cooked and the rolls are tender.

dishes.name: Goulash
dishes.description: Hungarian paprika-spiced beef and vegetable stew.
steps: Sauté onion until deeply softened.
Add paprika and stir briefly (careful not to burn it).
Add beef and brown lightly, then add enough water or stock to cover.
Simmer covered for 1.5 hours until the beef is nearly tender, then add potato and caraway.
Continue simmering until the potato is tender and the stew has thickened.

dishes.name: Lángos
dishes.description: Deep-fried Hungarian flatbread, often topped with sour cream and cheese.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, and mashed potato with warm water into a soft dough, then let rise about an hour.
Stretch portions of dough into flat rounds.
Deep fry each round in hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides.
Rub the hot langos with a cut garlic clove.
Top with sour cream and shredded cheese if desired.

dishes.name: Trdelník
dishes.description: Spit-rolled pastry dough coated in cinnamon sugar, popular street food.
steps: Make a sweet yeasted dough with flour, milk, sugar, and yeast, then let it rise.
Roll into long ropes and wrap each around a wooden spit or rolling pin.
Roll the wrapped dough in sugar and cinnamon.
Grill or bake over rotating heat until golden and crisp outside.
Slide off the spit and serve warm.

dishes.name: Kielbasa
dishes.description: Smoked Polish sausage eaten on its own or in stews.
steps: Mix ground and finely cubed pork with garlic, marjoram, and seasoning.
Stuff the mixture into casings, twisting into links.
Smoke or simmer the sausages until cooked through.
Finish by grilling or pan-searing until the skin is browned and crisp.
Serve with mustard and rye bread.

dishes.name: Smørrebrød
dishes.description: Open-faced Danish sandwich, artfully topped with fish, meat, or cheese.
steps: Spread a thin, even layer of butter on each slice of rye bread.
Arrange a chosen topping (smoked fish, roast beef, or egg) neatly over the bread.
Add complementary garnishes like dill, pickles, or radish slices.
Keep the toppings visually arranged rather than piled.
Serve open-faced, eaten with a knife and fork.

dishes.name: Köttbullar
dishes.description: Swedish meatballs served with a creamy sauce and tart lingonberry jam.
steps: Soak breadcrumbs in cream until softened.
Mix with ground meat, egg, and grated onion, then form into small round meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in butter until browned all over and cooked through.
Make a pan sauce with the drippings, cream, and a little stock.
Serve the meatballs with the sauce and lingonberry jam on the side.

dishes.name: Gravlax
dishes.description: Cured raw salmon flavored with dill, salt, and sugar.
steps: Mix salt and sugar together.
Rub the mixture generously over both sides of the salmon.
Pack fresh dill on top of the fish.
Wrap tightly and refrigerate under a weight for 48-72 hours, turning occasionally.
Scrape off the cure, slice thinly on an angle, and serve with mustard sauce.

dishes.name: Lutefisk
dishes.description: Traditional Norwegian dish of whitefish preserved and rehydrated with lye.
steps: Soak the dried fish in plain water for several days, changing the water daily, to soften it.
Soak the fish in a lye solution for a few days until it becomes gelatinous.
Soak again in fresh water for several more days to remove the lye completely.
Poach or bake the prepared fish gently until just cooked through.
Serve with melted butter, boiled potatoes, and peas.

dishes.name: Shakshuka
dishes.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and add diced onion and bell pepper, cooking until softened, about 6-8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cumin, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

Add crushed tomatoes and let the sauce simmer, stirring occasionally, for 12-15 minutes until it thickens noticeably — it should reduce from watery into something thick enough to hold its shape when you make a well in it.
Season the sauce with salt and a pinch of chili flakes if you want heat.
Using the back of a spoon, make several small wells in the sauce, spaced apart for each egg.
Crack an egg directly into each well.
Cover the skillet and cook over low heat for 5-8 minutes, checking periodically — you want the whites fully set but yolks still soft, so don't walk away too long.
Finish with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro scattered over the top.
Serve immediately, straight from the skillet, with warm crusty bread for scooping.

dishes.name: Sabich
dishes.description: Israeli pita sandwich built around fried eggplant and egg.
steps: Slice eggplant into rounds about a third of an inch thick.
Salt the slices generously and let them sit 20 minutes to draw out moisture and bitterness, then pat dry.
Fry the eggplant in oil over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and soft all the way through — check by pressing gently with a fork.
Drain the fried eggplant on paper towels.
Hard boil eggs (about 9-10 minutes for a fully set yolk) then peel and slice them.
Warm the pita bread briefly so it's soft and pliable.
Spread a generous layer of tahini sauce inside each pita.
Layer in the fried eggplant and sliced hard-boiled egg.
Add pickled vegetables and a spoonful of amba (pickled mango sauce) if you have it.
Serve immediately while the eggplant is still warm.

dishes.name: Maqluba
dishes.description: Layered rice and meat dish flipped upside down for serving, its name means 'upside-down'.
steps: Fry eggplant and cauliflower slices separately in oil until golden on both sides, then set aside on paper towels.
In the bottom of a large, heavy pot, brown chicken pieces with a mix of spices until nicely colored on all sides.
Remove the meat temporarily and layer the fried eggplant and cauliflower over the bottom of the pot.
Return the browned meat, arranging it over the vegetables.
Rinse basmati rice well, then spread it evenly over the meat as the top layer.
Carefully pour in stock or water until it just covers the rice by about half an inch.
Bring to a boil, reduce to very low, cover tightly, and cook undisturbed for about 30-40 minutes, until tender.
Let the pot rest off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes — this makes the flip much cleaner.
Place a large platter over the pot, and holding both firmly, flip the entire pot upside down in one confident motion. Lift the pot away carefully.
Don't worry if it isn't perfectly intact — even a messy flip tastes the same. Serve with yogurt on the side.

dishes.name: Mansaf
dishes.description: Jordan's national dish: lamb cooked in a tangy fermented yogurt sauce over rice.
steps: Simmer lamb pieces in water with onion until very tender, about 1.5-2 hours — reserve this broth for the next step.
Dissolve jameed (fermented dried yogurt) in the reserved broth, whisking continuously until smooth — add it gradually while whisking to avoid clumps.
Once smooth, gently simmer the sauce over low heat, stirring occasionally so it doesn't separate.
Add the cooked lamb to the sauce and simmer together for 20-30 minutes.
Cook rice separately until fluffy.
Spread a layer of flatbread across a large serving platter.
Spoon the rice over the flatbread in an even layer.
Arrange the lamb over the rice.
Ladle the warm sauce generously over everything.
Scatter toasted almonds or pine nuts on top and serve family-style, eating directly from the shared platter.

dishes.name: Kibbeh
dishes.description: Torpedo-shaped fried croquettes of bulgur and spiced minced meat.
steps: Soak fine bulgur in water for about 20 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as possible using a clean towel — wet bulgur makes the shell too soft to hold its shape while frying.
Blend the soaked bulgur with half your ground lamb, onion, and spices until it forms a smooth, sticky paste that holds together — this is your outer shell mixture.
For the filling, cook the remaining lamb with diced onion and pine nuts until browned, seasoning well.
Wet your hands and shape a portion of the shell mixture into a ball.
Press a deep hollow into the center with your thumb, working the mixture up the sides into a thin, even shell — this takes practice, so don't worry if the first few are uneven.
Spoon filling into the hollow, then pinch the top closed and reshape into a torpedo or oval.
Heat oil for deep-frying to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kibbeh in batches for 4-5 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp outside.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with yogurt dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Kabsa
dishes.description: Saudi Arabia's spiced rice and meat dish, similar to biryani.
steps: Brown chicken or lamb pieces with kabsa spice blend.
Sauté onion, garlic, and tomato in the same pot.
Add rice and stock, stirring to combine.
Nestle the meat back into the pot, cover, and cook until the rice is tender.
Fluff and serve topped with toasted nuts and raisins.

dishes.name: Mandi
dishes.description: Yemeni rice and meat dish traditionally slow-cooked in an underground pit.
steps: Rub the meat generously with mandi spice blend and let it marinate.
Slow-cook or smoke the meat until very tender, traditionally in an underground pit or tandoor.
Cook rice with saffron and some of the meat drippings for flavor and color.
Shred or portion the cooked meat.
Serve the meat over the fragrant rice.

dishes.name: Machboos
dishes.description: Spiced rice dish common across the Gulf, similar to biryani and kabsa.
steps: Brown the meat with onion and baharat spice blend.
Add dried lime and enough water to cover, then simmer until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat and cook rice in the same spiced broth.
Return the meat to the pot or layer it over the rice.
Serve hot with a side salad or yogurt sauce.

dishes.name: İskender Kebab
dishes.description: Sliced doner meat over pita, topped with tomato sauce, butter, and yogurt.
steps: If making the meat from scratch, marinate thin lamb or beef slices in yogurt and spices, then roast until you can shave off thin crispy-edged pieces — well-seasoned grilled thin lamb works as a home substitute.
Cut pita bread into cubes and layer them in the bottom of a serving dish.
Warm the tomato sauce until simmering.
Arrange the sliced meat over the bread cubes.
Pour the tomato sauce evenly over the meat and bread, letting it soak into the pita.
Melt butter in a small pan until it just begins to brown and smell nutty — this browning step adds real depth.
Pour the hot, sizzling browned butter over the top right before serving — it should sizzle audibly as it hits the plate.
Add a dollop of yogurt to one side.
Serve immediately while everything is hot.

dishes.name: Pide
dishes.description: Turkish flatbread shaped like a boat, topped and baked until crisp.
steps: Make a soft, slightly enriched dough with flour, yeast, warm water, and olive oil, kneading until smooth. Let rise about an hour, until doubled.
Divide the risen dough and roll each portion into an oval, thicker in the center, thinner at the edges.
